note: Tolerance bands for the three-way differential (GOAL-NATIVE-BOG.md D3). A band is a pyfunnel funnel: atolx seconds of time tolerance and atoly of value tolerance around the reference trajectory. Widening any value here needs a decision record under docs/decisions/ with an engineering rationale; the differential report names the band it applied. Because a trajectory may lead the reference by atolx, its last atolx seconds are not judged (the reference has no later point to match).

numeric.rationale: Module PIDs and timers integrate every execution period (1 s) while the IR and the reference step once per scan, so a continuous output leads by up to one scan and carries up to one scan of integral action (1.1 % of range at the Tier 1 loop gains, measured); requests and alarms derived from thresholds then move by up to two scans. Two percent of the signal's range and two scans cover this; the coarse-module-tick leg must agree within one scan and 0.1 %. docs/decisions/008. The range is taken over the whole suite; for a dimensionless signal (a fraction or a count) the scale is max(range, |max|).

boolean.rationale: Edges follow threshold crossings that may move by up to two scans under the execution-period difference; a boolean never differs in value once aligned. docs/decisions/008.

integer.rationale: Request counts and alarm levels are integers; only their timing may move, by up to two scans. docs/decisions/008.

coarse.note: Bands for the coarse-module-tick leg, where every module component steps once per scan like the IR: values must agree to 0.1 % of range (1e-9 floor) and timing within one scan, the same one-scan ordering slack the IR and the Open Control Engine need between themselves.

numeric.rationale: Same discretisation as the IR; any difference is a semantic disagreement. Same scale rule as the default set.

scan.note: Bands for the scan-module-tick leg (module period equal to the case's scan, whatever the scan): values as the coarse leg, timing within three scans, because every module kernel in a chain ticks once per scan in document order, so an edge that crosses a chain of Pre, TimerAccumulating and SetReset kernels lands up to three scans later than in the IR (measured on the Tier 3 hot water plant's runtime rotation). docs/decisions/011.

numeric.rationale: Same discretisation as the IR; any difference is a semantic disagreement. Same scale rule as the default set. Scan leg: three scans of timing slack for module-kernel chains (docs/decisions/011).

boolean.rationale: Same discretisation as the IR. Scan leg: three scans of timing slack for module-kernel chains (docs/decisions/011).

integer.rationale: Same discretisation as the IR. Scan leg: three scans of timing slack for module-kernel chains (docs/decisions/011).
